test_title: PYST 7: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following programmes was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) in 2019 to improve air quality in 131 cities (non-attainment cities and million plus cities) across 24 states/UTs?

options.text: National Association of Clean Air Agencies

solution:
The correct answer is __**National Clean Air Program**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Program (NCAP):**

 
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)** launched the **National Clean Air Program** in **2019**.
 
• The program aims to improve **air quality** across **131 cities**, known as **non-attainment cities** and **million-plus cities**, in **24 states and UTs**.
 
• Non-attainment cities are those that do not meet the prescribed **national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS)**.
 
• The NCAP provides a **time-bound plan** to reduce pollution levels by **20-30%** by **2024**, compared to 2017 levels.
 
• Focus areas include reducing pollution from sectors like **transportation, industries, waste management, construction, and biomass burning**.
 
• The program emphasizes **capacity building, monitoring networks, community participation, and technology interventions**.
 
• The NCAP also promotes collaboration with **state governments, local bodies, and relevant stakeholders**.
 
 
 
• The goal is to ensure better **air quality management** and create awareness among citizens regarding **air pollution**.
 
• This initiative is aligned with India’s commitment to reduce emissions under the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is National Clean Air Program.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Options in the Question:**

 
 
• **Swach Bayu Sarvekshan:**

 
 
• Not an actual program launched by the government, but could refer to any survey aimed at measuring cleanliness or air quality.
 
• This option is incorrect as it does not align with the **2019 initiative by MoEF&CC**.
 
 
 
• **National Association of Clean Air Agencies:**
 
 
• This is an organization based in the **United States** that focuses on **air pollution control**.
 
• Since it is not an Indian initiative, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Air Quality Forecasting System:**
 
 
• This refers to systems designed to predict air quality levels, but it is not a specific program launched by MoEF&CC in **2019**.
 
• It is a part of air pollution control measures but does not represent the **National Clean Air Program**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Air Pollution in India:**
 
 
• Air pollution is a significant challenge in India, with major cities like **Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai** often exceeding **NAAQS** limits.
 
• Sources include **vehicular emissions, industrial discharge, construction activities, waste burning, and natural factors**.
 
• Efforts like the NCAP aim to address these issues comprehensively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation:**

 
 
• The NCAP involves the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** and state pollution control boards for monitoring and implementation.
 
• It prioritizes cities with high pollution levels to ensure targeted action.
 
• **Monitoring stations** have been increased across the country for better data collection and analysis.
 
 
 
• **International Comparisons:**
 
 
• Similar programs exist globally, such as **China’s Blue Sky Action Plan** and the **Clean Air Act in the USA**.
 
• These efforts highlight the global nature of tackling air pollution and its importance for public health.
 
 
 
• **Health Impact:**
 
 
• Air pollution contributes to respiratory diseases like **asthma, bronchitis**, and cardiovascular issues.
 
• Reducing pollution has direct benefits for improving **public health and life expectancy**.
